# Build odu's outputs and push their closures to the shared Attic cache
# (https://cache.nixos.asia/oss) — and then publish the lane runner
# CONTENT-ADDRESSED, so a dial from a published revision has the host pull its
# own build with NO trust (`@kolu/surface-remote`'s `provisionAgent` index step;
# the publisher is `juspay/kolu`'s `publish-closure` action, pinned to the kolu
# revision odu pins in `npins/sources.json`).
#
# Two jobs, because they are two halves of one question with one ordering:
# `build-and-push` warms the input-addressed cache a lane host substitutes from,
# and `publish-closures` then rewrites from that same tree. It must be its OWN
# job: the action installs the Nix it rewrites with (2.34.8 — see its
# `action.yml`), which has to be the job's only Nix.
#
# `odu`'s `ca-index` branch is born on the first master push. A pull request
# rewrites, smokes and import-verifies, and writes no index.
name: nix-cache

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least privilege — only the publish job needs more, and it asks for it itself.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: nix-cache-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # ubuntu-latest → x86_64-linux; macos-latest → aarch64-darwin. Both are
        # platforms odu's own required checks (ci::*) run on, so both are
        # platforms whose closures a lane actually provisions.
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      # `ref:` is LOAD-BEARING on `pull_request`. actions/checkout defaults to
      # `github.ref`, which for that event is `refs/pull/N/merge` — a synthetic
      # merge of the PR into its base that NOTHING else ever builds. Developers
      # and odu's own lanes build the branch head, so warming the merge tree
      # leaves the tree everybody wants cold. `head.sha` is empty on non-PR
      # events, where checkout's own default is already the right tree. (This is
      # kolu#2101 F5(a)'s correction, kept here for the same reason.)
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      # Pinned by commit (CodeQL: unpinned third-party action). v35 → 9f63be7.
      # Nix 2.34.7 here; the publish job installs 2.34.8 for the rewrite — see
      # its action. This job only builds and pushes, which either line does.
      - uses: nixbuild/nix-quick-install-action@9f63be77f412a248c9d9a65a4c82cf066cdf8f0c # v35
        with:
          nix_conf: |
            extra-substituters = https://cache.nixos.asia/oss
            extra-trusted-public-keys = oss:KO872wNJkCDgmGN3xy9dT89WAhvv13EiKncTtHDItVU=
            accept-flake-config = true

      # ONE step, not a step per branch, so the token is never consulted in an
      # `if`. A pull request with no token still BUILDS — that is the check this
      # workflow owes a PR — and pushes nothing. A push with no token FAILS: a
      # push is where this job is required to publish, and going green having
      # warmed nothing is precisely the state a cache job exists to make
      # impossible (kolu's nix-cache.yml states the rule).
      #
      # attic is installed from the repo's own npins-pinned nixpkgs, not an
      # unpinned ref resolved through the GitHub API at run time: that API
      # returning 503 is a repo-wide failure mode, and the tarball URL
      # `nix/nixpkgs.nix` already builds from needs no resolution at all.
      - name: Build odu's outputs, and push their closures
        env:
          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          paths=$(nix build -L --no-link --print-out-paths --accept-flake-config \
            .#odu .#odu-runner .#web-ui)
          # A positive assertion, not dressing: a build that produced nothing
          # would otherwise push nothing and still report success.
          if [ -z "$paths" ]; then
            echo "::error::nix build produced no output paths"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$ATTIC_TOKEN" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
              echo "::error::ATTIC_TOKEN is not set on $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — this push would publish no closure and no ca-index entry. Add the secret (the same attic login juspay/kolu uses)."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "no ATTIC_TOKEN (a pull request) — built, pushed nothing"
            exit 0
          fi
          nix profile add "$(jq -r .pins.nixpkgs.url npins/sources.json)#attic-client"
          attic login --set-default oss https://cache.nixos.asia "$ATTIC_TOKEN"
          # `attic push` defaults to pushing CLOSURES and to skipping what
          # cache.nixos.org already serves, so the out-paths alone are the
          # complete instruction and nixpkgs stays out of a project cache.
          printf '%s\n' "$paths" | attic push --stdin oss

  publish-closures:
    needs: build-and-push
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Writes the `ca-index` branch of this repository.
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The same tree `build-and-push` warmed — see its `ref:` note.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      # attic, for the action's push, from the same pinned nixpkgs the build
      # job installs it from — one pin, read the same way.
      - id: inputs
        run: |
          echo "nixpkgs=$(jq -r .pins.nixpkgs.url npins/sources.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # odu's declaration is `.#agent-flake-source`'s own sidecar + commit-hash
      # (the same derivation the `odu` wrapper bakes), so the action reads them
      # rather than being told. `odu-runner` is the ONE attr a remote resolves.
      # The smoke runs out of the REWRITTEN closure: `--help` loads the runner's
      # whole module graph and exits 0 without needing stdin, which `--stdio`
      # would (it serves until the pipe closes).
      #
      # The pin is kolu's merged head, whose `.gitattributes` keeps
      # `.github/actions` in the archive a remote `uses:` is downloaded from —
      # before that it was export-ignored, and this step died at job setup with
      # "Can't find 'action.yml'".
      - uses: juspay/kolu/.github/actions/publish-closure@5b14790a4eb9c383dfd7fa247bbff1af60f9eb92
        with:
          source: .#agent-flake-source
          installables: odu-runner
          latest: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' }}
          smoke: |
            odu-runner=bin/odu-runner --help
          attic-nixpkgs: ${{ steps.inputs.outputs.nixpkgs }}
          attic-token: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}

/**
 * The argv every Chromium this package launches is launched with.
 *
 * ONE list, because the reason for each flag is about where the browser RUNS and
 * not about what it is being asked to do: under Nix, in a container, on a CI
 * runner with no display and a small `/dev/shm`. Every one of them is
 * load-bearing there and harmless on a laptop, which is why the same argv is
 * used everywhere rather than branched on `CI` — a browser configured
 * differently in CI than on a laptop is a class of bug that only ever
 * reproduces where it is hardest to debug. `--disable-dev-shm-usage` is the one
 * whose absence is quietest: without it a browser on a 64 MB `/dev/shm` dies
 * mid-run, and what the suite reports is a page that stopped answering.
 *
 * It lives in its own module rather than beside the launch in `./hooks.ts`,
 * because importing that module REGISTERS cucumber hooks — a driver that is not
 * the suite cannot reach for the argv without also enrolling itself in a run.
 * This file imports nothing at all, so anything can share it.
 */
export const BROWSER_ARGS: ReadonlyArray<string> = [
  "--no-sandbox",
  "--disable-setuid-sandbox",
  "--disable-gpu",
  "--disable-dev-shm-usage",
  "--headless=new",
];

# E2E tests

Black-box end-to-end tests: build the real `odu` binary with Nix, run it
against a throwaway fixture repo on a **localhost lane**, and assert on its
`--progress json` stream and process exit code.

These cover the seams the in-process loopback suite (`src/odu.test.ts`) stubs:
just-DAG ingest → scheduling → local lane spawn (`odu-runner`) → NDJSON
projection → exit code.

## Layout

```
tests/e2e/
├── harness.ts            # nix build, fixture materialization, run + parse
├── run.e2e.test.ts       # the run assertions (bun:test)
├── cancel.e2e.test.ts    # cancel / supersede / linger, driven from a 2nd process
├── protect.e2e.test.ts   # `odu protect --dry-run` context enumeration
├── mcp.e2e.test.ts       # the `odu mcp` agent face over a real MCP client
├── logs.e2e.test.ts      # durable node logs: complete to the last line, one run per file
├── webHarness.ts         # a real web service in a private world (HOME, state, port)
├── web.e2e.test.ts       # the CROSS-FACE gate: one run through the CLI, the
│                         # HTTP MCP face and the singleton
├── fixtures/
│   ├── pass/justfile     # a DAG that goes green
│   ├── fail/justfile     # a DAG whose node fails (exit 1)
│   ├── sleep/justfile    # a DAG that stays running, to cancel out from under
│   └── noisy/justfile    # a DAG that outruns the log wire, then exits at once
└── README.md
```

Run locally:

```sh
bun run test:e2e-cli     # bun test tests/e2e
just e2e-cli             # the same suite, against a freshly nix-built odu
just e2e                 # BOTH end-to-end suites: this one and e2e-web
```

In CI it's the `e2e-cli` step in `ci/mod.just`. The browser suite is `e2e-web`
beside it; the two are one gate with two drivers, which is what the names say.

## How a fixture works

A fixture is just a throwaway git repo with a `justfile` — **no flake**. The
coordinator resolves its lane runner from the agent source baked into the
`.#odu` binary under test (`SURFACE_AGENT_FLAKE_REF` — odu's own tree, assembled
by `default.nix`; the resolver is
`packages/execution/src/coordinator/runnerFlake.ts`), *not* from the repo under
test. So a fixture re-exports nothing: it stands in for a real consumer that
runs odu without exporting `odu-runner` — exactly the cross-repo path
[#30](https://github.com/juspay/odu/issues/30) fixed. (Even for a localhost lane
the realise is a local no-op copy, but the `drvPath` lookup still runs — now
against the baked source, a Nix cache hit since the harness builds `.#odu`
first.)

The leaf recipes are pure shell — the fixture's own "CI" is trivial on purpose,
so the test exercises *odu's* machinery, not a real toolchain.

## The cross-face gate

`web.e2e.test.ts` is the one suite that can check the property the web release
rests on: a start, a wait, a log read, a retry and a cancel produce the **same
addressed state** whichever door they came through, and the three outcomes
(answered · refused · nothing serving) stay apart at each one. It cannot be a
unit test, because every one of those doors is a separate process.

Its world is private on purpose — `ODU_STATE_DIR`, `ODU_WEB_ORIGIN` and the port
are all per-suite — so it does not touch a developer's own running `odu web`, and
two copies of the suite on one machine do not fight over a gate. `HOME` is
deliberately *not* redirected; `webHarness.ts` records the CI-only failure that
taught us why.

**The browser is not one of the doors this suite drives.** It used to be: three
cases shelled out to `chrome --headless --dump-dom` and asserted on substrings of
one static snapshot — no click, no keystroke, no viewport, no reconnect — and
skipped themselves where no browser was on PATH, so on a CI runner they graded
nothing at all.

That coverage now lives in [`packages/web-acceptance`](../../packages/web-acceptance/README.md):
Gherkin scenarios driven through Playwright, against this same nix-built binary,
with the browsers supplied by nixpkgs. It is a **required** leg on both platforms
(`ci/mod.just`'s `e2e-web`) and it never skips — a machine with no
browsers fails it with the sentence that gets them.

## Deliberate tradeoffs

- **The harness builds the binary itself** (`nix build .#odu .#odu-runner`)
  rather than assuming a pre-built `./result`. This makes the suite
  self-contained and order-independent, at the cost of a cold-cache build on
  the first run (hence the 10-minute `beforeAll` timeout). Subsequent runs are
  cache hits.
- **Assertions read `--progress json` (NDJSON), not the TTY dashboard.** The
  dashboard is a separate rendering path; asserting on the clean, parseable
  stream keeps tests robust. The dashboard is currently uncovered by e2e.
- **Local-only.** No remote/ssh lanes are exercised; fixtures run on a
  localhost lane against a working-tree snapshot (`--no-strict`).
- **Black-box.** `harness.ts` imports nothing from `src/` — the contract under
  test is the binary's observable behavior, so internal refactors don't ripple
  into these tests.
- **No separate runner config.** These suites need far longer deadlines than a
  unit test and must not run concurrently with each other — a fixture binds the
  one-run lock and `.ci/odu.sock` in its own repo, but two suites racing the
  same nix build and the same machine is how this suite used to flake. Both
  facts are now stated where they apply rather than in a config file: each
  `it`/`beforeAll` names its own timeout as a trailing argument, and `bun test`
  already runs test *files* one at a time. So `bun test tests/e2e` needs no
  flags beyond the path.

## Follow-ups

- Cover the **TTY dashboard** / `attach` live view (PTY-driven).
- Exercise a **real transport**: an ssh-to-localhost lane to cover the
  `nix copy` → remote realise → spawn-over-ssh path that localhost
  short-circuits.
- Drive the **MCP agent face** (`odu mcp`) end-to-end as a subprocess.
- Drive `odu mcp --service` (the stdio bridge to the singleton) as a subprocess;
  the HTTP face of the same projection is covered.
- Cover `status -o json` and `logs -f` against a live run (they need the
  `.ci/odu.sock` socket, so the harness would run `odu run` in the background
  and dial it concurrently).
- **Multi-platform fanout** once remote lanes are in scope.

`dirty.e2e.test.ts` exercises working-tree capture and chunked git-bundle transport over the real localhost stdio surface using `ODU_SNAPSHOT_TRANSPORT=always` and a private `file://` origin. Real SSH host acceptance remains downstream in Olai. Cache-hit assertions repeat identical content, separately from red-to-green edits.

name: Deploy website to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [master, website]
    paths:
      - "website/**"
      - ".github/workflows/pages.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Build and upload website
        # Pinned to a commit rather than a mutable tag — see the note in
        # ci.yml; this job builds and publishes the public site.
        uses: withastro/action@e84f40bd8d2caa9e768ec82ad30dd81f0b280853 # v6
        with:
          path: website
          node-version: 24
          package-manager: npm@latest

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

{
  "name": "odu",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "license": "AGPL-3.0-or-later",
  "type": "module",
  "//workspaces": "Each member is a WALL, not a folder, and the walls run ONE WAY: cli → execution → run-history → run-client. run-client is the half of odu a client of a LIVE run holds; run-history is everything that OUTLIVES a coordinator (the per-user catalog, the journal, per-attempt evidence, and the checkout-scoped ledger as its legacy half); execution is everything that DOES a run; cli is the two ways of WATCHING one (the native CLI/TUI and the MCP surface). PR 2 adds three more, and the arrow still runs one way: service-client is the CONTRACT the web service serves (browser-safe by construction — its closure test refuses a `node:` import); service is what IMPLEMENTS it, and it cannot import execution, so the three things it must cause — launch, retry, cancel — arrive as ports the root binds; web-ui is the browser, which holds views and no domain logic at all. What is left in src/ is the composition roots — main.ts and runner-main.ts — the only place the faces and the engine are wired to each other. Each member's src/closure.test.ts walks its own import graph, so the direction is physics rather than discipline. Every member is also listed in `dependencies` below: the isolated linker symlinks only the root package's DIRECT dependencies into the root node_modules, so without those entries `@odu/*` would not resolve from src/.",
  "workspaces": [
    "packages/*"
  ],
  "scripts": {
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test:unit": "bun test ./src ./packages",
    "test:e2e-cli": "bun test ./tests/e2e"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@odu/cli": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/execution": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/run-client": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/run-history": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/service": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/service-client": "workspace:*",
    "@effect/platform-browser": "4.0.0",
    "@effect/platform-node": "4.0.0",
    "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "^1.29.0",
    "@opentui/core": "^0.4.5",
    "@preact/signals-core": "^1.8.0",
    "@solid-primitives/rootless": "^1.5.3",
    "@solid-primitives/scheduled": "^1.5.3",
    "@xterm/headless": "^6.0.0",
    "dequal": "^2.0.3",
    "effect": "4.0.0",
    "neverthrow": "^8.2.0",
    "quick-lru": "^7.3.0",
    "solid-js": "^1.9.15",
    "split2": "^4.2.0",
    "ts-pattern": "^5.9.0",
    "ws": "^8.21.0"
  },
  "//overrides": "One effect instance, always. The @kolu/* sources are hydrated from the Nix store and resolve `effect` by walking up to this root node_modules (bunfig.toml explains the isolated-linker invariant), so a second copy arriving transitively would give kolu's _tag-based error narrowing two class realms to disagree about.",
  "overrides": {
    "effect": "4.0.0",
    "@effect/platform-node": "4.0.0",
    "@effect/platform-browser": "4.0.0"
  },
  "//devDependencies": "The three babel entries are the SOLID COMPILER, and they are a build-time toolchain rather than a runtime dependency: `scripts/build-web-ui.ts` runs them over `packages/web-ui`'s `.tsx` before Bun bundles the result, and nothing ships them. They are pinned EXACTLY, without a caret, for the same reason `@odu/web-acceptance` pins playwright: this compiler decides whether the browser gets Solid's fine-grained updates or a React-shaped re-render of whole components, and that is not a property to let float on a patch release. `babel-preset-solid` peers `solid-js` exactly, so the two move together.",
  "devDependencies": {
    "@babel/core": "7.29.7",
    "@babel/preset-typescript": "7.29.7",
    "babel-preset-solid": "1.9.15",
    "@types/bun": "^1.2.0",
    "@types/node": "^22.0.0",
    "@types/split2": "^4.2.3",
    "@types/ws": "^8.18.1",
    "typescript": "^5.8.0"
  }
}

{
  "name": "@odu/run-history",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "license": "AGPL-3.0-or-later",
  "type": "module",
  "//": "THE DURABLE RUN CATALOG \u2014 see README.md, which argues the boundary. This package owns what outlives a coordinator: the per-user catalog, the ordered journal, immutable per-attempt evidence, the ownership fence, and the one attention query every face asks. It depends on @odu/run-client (the wire vocabulary a run speaks) and on nothing else of odu, so `execution` and `cli` can both read history without either importing the other.",
  "//dependencies": "`@odu/run-client` is a workspace sibling, and the arrow runs one way: run-history \u2192 run-client, never back. `effect` must stay at the version the rest of the tree resolves (the root `overrides` pins it) \u2014 two copies give Effect's _tag-based narrowing two class realms to disagree about, and the symptom is a decode failure on a well-formed record. src/closure.test.ts walks the import graph to keep both facts true.",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "exports": {
    "./ids": "./src/ids.ts",
    "./schema": "./src/schema.ts",
    "./exit": "./src/exit.ts",
    "./paths": "./src/paths.ts",
    "./attention": "./src/attention.ts",
    "./store": "./src/store.ts",
    "./owner": "./src/owner.ts",
    "./query": "./src/query.ts",
    "./receipts": "./src/receipts.ts",
    "./reconcile": "./src/reconcile.ts",
    "./retention": "./src/retention.ts",
    "./import": "./src/import.ts",
    "./legacy/record": "./src/legacy/record.ts",
    "./legacy/ledger": "./src/legacy/ledger.ts"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@odu/run-client": "workspace:*",
    "effect": "4.0.0"
  }
}

{
  "name": "@odu/cli",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "license": "AGPL-3.0-or-later",
  "type": "module",
  "//": "THE FACES — see README.md. The native CLI and its TUI, and the MCP agent surface. Both are ways of WATCHING a run and asking things of one; neither is how a run happens. The arrow runs cli → execution and never back, which is what lets a service face be built over the engine in PR 2 without a terminal emulator in its closure.",
  "//exports": "A subpath pattern, for the reason `@odu/execution` gives: this package ships from this tree with its only consumer (`src/main.ts`), so a curated surface here would be a list nobody reads rather than a promise somebody depends on.",
  "//dependencies": "The renderer and terminal packages are REAL installs and the reason this package exists as a separate wall: `@opentui/core` and `@xterm/headless` are a renderer and a terminal emulator, and an engine that carried them in its closure could not be served from anything but a terminal. `@effect/platform-node` arrives with PR 2's argv face — the generated CLI's process edge is `NodeRuntime.runMain`, and the face's exit discipline is only true of a real binary. `@odu/service` and `@odu/service-client` are the web service and its contract: this package composes them (the daemon, the argv projection, the MCP bridge) and binds their ports to the engine, which is the one place the two are wired to each other. The @kolu/* sources are hydrated from a Nix pin and so are absent here by design — see the note in @odu/execution's manifest, and src/closure.test.ts, which pins the hydrated set.",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "exports": {
    "./*": "./src/*.ts"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@effect/platform-node": "4.0.0",
    "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "^1.29.0",
    "@odu/execution": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/run-client": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/run-history": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/service": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/service-client": "workspace:*",
    "@opentui/core": "^0.4.5",
    "@xterm/headless": "^6.0.0",
    "effect": "4.0.0"
  }
}

{
  "name": "@odu/service-client",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "license": "AGPL-3.0-or-later",
  "type": "module",
  "//": "WHAT A CLIENT OF THE ODU SERVICE HOLDS — see README.md. The typed contract the singleton web service serves, the shared verb table every face projects it through, and the dial that reaches it. It is the browser's half AND the generated CLI's half AND the MCP bridge's half, which is the whole reason it is a package: three faces that agreed by convention would be three faces that drift. It knows nothing about how a run happens, where the catalog is, or what a coordinator is — those are @odu/service's, one wall up.",
  "//dependencies": "BROWSER-SAFE, and the manifest is the promise. `@odu/run-history` is here for its PORTABLE half alone — `./schema` (the durable record shapes this surface re-publishes) and `./ids` (the cursor/attempt/node-key spellings a caller echoes back) — never its `./store` platform I/O; src/closure.test.ts pins exactly which subpaths are reached. `@odu/run-client` comes along for the node-status vocabulary `schema` itself reads. The @kolu/* sources are hydrated as raw TypeScript from a Nix pin (see bunfig.toml at the root), so naming one here would send bun to the registry for a package that is not there — the closure test pins the hydrated set instead.",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "exports": {
    "./surface": "./src/surface.ts",
    "./verbs": "./src/verbs.ts",
    "./endpoint": "./src/endpoint.ts",
    "./logKey": "./src/logKey.ts",
    "./dial": "./src/dial.ts",
    "./socket": "./src/socket.ts",
    "./board": "./src/board.ts",
    "./routes": "./src/routes.ts"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@odu/run-client": "workspace:*",
    "@odu/run-history": "workspace:*",
    "effect": "4.0.0"
  }
}

{
  "name": "@odu/run-client",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-populate the nix store with crates.io tarballs that nixpkgs' fetchurl
# can't download. crates.io's anti-bot layer returns HTTP 403 for requests
# carrying a `curl/*` User-Agent — the default for nixpkgs fetchurl — which
# blocks every `crate-*.tar.gz` fixed-output derivation in this project's cargo
# vendor closure. Measured 2026-08-27:
#
#     curl -A 'curl/8.5.0'  .../crates/cucumber/0.23.0/download  -> 403
#     curl -A 'Mozilla/5.0' .../crates/cucumber/0.23.0/download  -> 200
#
# `NIX_CURL_FLAGS` is listed in fetchurl's `impureEnvVars`, but it is read from
# the BUILD DAEMON's environment, so neither exporting it nor `--option
# impure-env` reaches the builder on a daemon install. Both were tried; both
# still 403.
#
# Workaround: fetch each missing crate with a non-curl UA, then inject the
# tarball into the local store with `nix-store --add-fixed sha256`. That yields
# a content-addressed path identical to the FOD's declared `outputHash`, so the
# subsequent `nix build` finds the artifact already realised and never touches
# the network for it.
#
# Idempotent: crates whose output is already valid in the store are skipped, so
# a warm store (or a populated substituter) makes this a few metadata lookups.
#
# Drop this script and its CI step once upstream nixpkgs sidesteps the UA
# filter (e.g. by fetching from `static.crates.io` directly).
#
# The Rust here is bun2nix itself: `ci::bun-nix-fresh` and
# `just regenerate-bun-nix` both `nix run .#bun2nix`, and on a runner whose
# store lacks it that means building askama / basic-toml / jsonc-parser and
# friends from crates.io. So that is the attribute walked.
#
# Shared, not duplicated by accident: juspay/drishti has carried this for its
# own bun2nix closure since 2026-05 and juspay/osfacts took it for a cargo
# package closure. This copy fixes two things the drishti original has: each
# download URL comes from the derivation's own `urls` attribute rather than
# being rebuilt from the store basename (rebuilding does not survive cargo's
# `+build` metadata), and the crate list is read from a file instead of piped
# into `while read`, so a failed fetch fails the recipe rather than exiting 0
# half-done.

set -euo pipefail

UA='Mozilla/5.0'
flake_root=${1:-.}

bun2nix_drv=$(nix eval --raw --accept-flake-config "${flake_root}#bun2nix.drvPath")
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

# Collect to a FILE first, then loop over it — a `while read` on the right of a
# pipe runs in a subshell, where `set -e` kills only that subshell and the
# script exits 0 with the work half done. A failed fetch must fail the CI step,
# not be swallowed. (A file rather than `mapfile`: macOS runners ship bash 3.2,
# which has no `mapfile`.)
list="$tmpdir/crate-drvs"
nix-store --query --requisites "$bun2nix_drv" | grep 'crate-.*\.tar\.gz\.drv$' > "$list" || true

total=$(wc -l < "$list" | tr -d ' ')
prefetched=0
while IFS= read -r cdrv; do
  [ -n "$cdrv" ] || continue
  out=$(nix-store --query --outputs "$cdrv")
  if nix-store --check-validity "$out" 2>/dev/null; then
    continue
  fi

  # `nix-store --add-fixed` names the store path after the FILE's basename, so
  # the temp file must be named as the store path is WITHOUT its hash prefix.
  # Naming it after the full basename mints `<newhash>-<oldhash>-crate-…`, a
  # path no fixed-output derivation is looking for, and the build then 403s
  # exactly as if nothing had been prefetched.
  store_name=$(basename "$out" | cut -d- -f2-)

  # PREFERRED: ask the derivation. Two shapes to survive — nix >= 2.31 wraps the
  # map in `.derivations`, and a `structuredAttrs` derivation carries `urls`
  # there rather than in `env`; `..|objects|.urls?` finds it either way, and
  # `env.url` is the unstructured fallback. stderr is captured rather than
  # dropped, so a `nix derivation show` that fails on some other nix build says
  # WHY instead of arriving here as a silent empty string.
  show_err="$tmpdir/show.err"
  url=$(
    nix derivation show "$cdrv" 2>"$show_err" \
      | jq -r '[.. | objects | (.urls? // empty)] + [.. | objects | (.env?.url? // empty)]
               | flatten
               | map(select(type == "string"))
               | map(split(" ")[]) | map(select(startswith("http")))
               | first // ""' 2>/dev/null
  )

  # FALLBACK: rebuild it from the store name. Correct-by-construction is not
  # possible here — a crate name may itself end in `-<digits>` — so this is a
  # heuristic: the version begins at the FIRST `-`-separated token that starts
  # with a digit, and runs to the end. That is what keeps cargo's `+build`
  # metadata intact (`wasip2-1.0.4+wasi-0.2.12` → name `wasip2`, version
  # `1.0.4+wasi-0.2.12`), where splitting on the LAST `-` would 404. A wrong
  # guess is not silent: the add-fixed assertion below compares the path we
  # minted against the path the FOD wants, and a wrong tarball cannot match it.
  if [ -z "$url" ]; then
    stem=${store_name%.tar.gz}
    stem=${stem#crate-}
    name=""; ver=""
    IFS='-' read -ra parts <<< "$stem"
    for i in "${!parts[@]}"; do
      case "${parts[$i]}" in
        [0-9]*)
          name=$(IFS='-'; echo "${parts[*]:0:$i}")
          ver=$(IFS='-'; echo "${parts[*]:$i}")
          break
          ;;
      esac
    done
    if [ -n "$name" ] && [ -n "$ver" ]; then
      url="https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$name/$ver/download"
      echo "note: rebuilt url for $store_name (derivation gave none)" >&2
    fi
  fi

  if [ -z "$url" ] || [ "$url" = "null" ]; then
    echo "no url for $cdrv" >&2
    echo "--- nix derivation show stderr ---" >&2
    cat "$show_err" >&2 || true
    exit 1
  fi

  tmp="$tmpdir/$store_name"
  curl -fsSL -A "$UA" -o "$tmp" "$url"
  added=$(nix-store --add-fixed sha256 "$tmp")

  # Self-check, because the failure mode above is silent: unless the path we
  # just added IS the FOD's output path, we have cached nothing useful.
  if [ "$added" != "$out" ]; then
    echo "prefetch landed at $added but the FOD wants $out" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "prefetched: $store_name"
  prefetched=$((prefetched + 1))
done < "$list"

echo "prefetched $prefetched crate(s); $total in closure"
